name: French
tagline: Every stall has a story. Every story has a word you need.
subject: French Language
description: A night market floats on the Seine, lit by paper lanterns. Each vendor speaks French — the baker, the flower seller, the old woman with the music box. Your guide Colette knows everyone. Every purchase, every conversation, every secret you overhear teaches you the language. By the end, the market feels like home.

companions.name: Colette
companions.personality: A young Parisian who loves her city's hidden corners. Warm, conspiratorial, treats the learner as a friend she's showing around. Makes French feel like a secret language only cool people speak.
companions.speech_pattern: Mixes French naturally, translates with a wink. Says 'Tu vois?' (You see?) when the learner gets it. Celebrates with 'Magnifique!' genuinely. Never makes the learner feel foreign.

domains.name: Market French
concepts: Greetings — bonjour, bonsoir, comment allez-vous
Numbers and prices — counting euros, asking combien
Food vocabulary — pain, fromage, pomme, chocolat, eau
Polite expressions — s'il vous plaît, merci, excusez-moi
Basic transactions — je voudrais, c'est combien, l'addition
domains.mastery_signal: Can greet a vendor, ask prices, order food, and complete a purchase entirely in French

domains.name: Conversation
concepts: Introducing yourself — je m'appelle, j'habite, j'ai X ans
Questions — qu'est-ce que, où, quand, pourquoi, comment
Describing things — adjectives, colors, sizes, feelings
Family and friends — ma famille, mon ami, frère, sœur
Daily routine — le matin, l'après-midi, le soir
domains.mastery_signal: Can have a 5-minute conversation about yourself, your family, and your day

domains.name: Grammar Through Use
concepts: Gender — le/la, masculine/feminine patterns
Present tense — être, avoir, aller, faire, vouloir, pouvoir
Negation — ne...pas, ne...jamais, ne...rien
Articles — un/une, du/de la, des
Past tense basics — passé composé with avoir
domains.mastery_signal: Can form correct present and simple past sentences, use the right articles, and negate naturally

domains.name: Reading & Writing
concepts: Reading menus, signs, and notes
French pronunciation rules — silent letters, liaisons, accents
Writing short messages and responses
Cognates and false friends
Simple story comprehension
domains.mastery_signal: Can read a French menu, write a short note, and follow a simple story

real_world_application: Navigate a French market, order food, have basic conversations, and read simple French text.
